destination.name: Armidale
destination.tagline: A university city on the Northern Tablelands with a regional art museum, a National Trust homestead and a heritage village close by.
destination.description: Armidale is a city of 23,967 people (2021 census) on the Northern Tablelands, about halfway between Sydney and Brisbane at the start of Waterfall Way to the coast. Visitors come for the New England Regional Art Museum, Saumarez Homestead's 30 furnished rooms and the heritage town of Uralla. Its altitude gives four distinct seasons, with trees in the town's gardens turning colour in autumn.
whyVisit: Explore heritage Uralla on the highway

goodToKnow.title: Saumarez by guided tour
goodToKnow.detail: The house is open by guided tour only; the gardens are open 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM Wednesday and Friday to Sunday, and entry is about $12 to $17.

goodToKnow.title: NERAM closed Mondays
goodToKnow.detail: The New England Regional Art Museum is open Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM, and entry is free.

goodToKnow.title: Cold winters
goodToKnow.detail: Wikivoyage reports very cold winters with overnight temperatures below freezing and occasional snow, so pack warm layers from June to August.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Come in {months}: Wikivoyage calls summer arguably the best time, rarely humid at this altitude, and autumn brings the town's colour change and Autumn Festival.
